Control options for Huber scree estimation

Source: R/scree.R
huber_control.Rd

Creates a control list for method = "huber" in dp_scree() or the scree configuration of dp_pca().

Usage

huber_control(
  k_min_m2,
  k_max_m2,
  m2_frac,
  mu0 = 0,
  eta0 = 1,
  T = NULL,
  M = NULL
)

Arguments

k_min_m2, k_max_m2

Required public integer bounds for the dyadic scale grid, with k_min_m2 < k_max_m2.

m2_frac

Required fraction in (0, 1) of epsilon used for the private scale step.

mu0

Public initial mean estimate (0 by default).

eta0

Positive public gradient step size (1 by default).

T

Number of gradient iterations; NULL (default) uses ceiling(log(m)), where m = floor(n / 2).

M

Number of scale-estimation blocks; NULL (default) uses floor(sqrt(m / 2)), capped by available input pairs.

Value

A control list for method = "huber".

Details

The Huber method privately estimates a robust scale for each component using a noisy dyadic histogram, then performs projected noisy gradient updates to estimate the mean of squared pair differences. The scale proxy sets the Huber threshold; it is not a raw second moment. At least eight observations are required.

The private scale step uses m2_frac * epsilon / k for each component and no delta. Joint gradient updates use the remaining epsilon and all delta, calibrated across components and iterations. Each update is projected to nonnegative values; optional monotone adjustment follows estimation. Tuning parameters must be public or have separate privacy accounting.

References

Yu M, Ren Z, Zhou W (2024). “Gaussian differentially private robust mean estimation and inference.” Bernoulli, 30(4), 3059–3088.

See also

dp_scree() for computing differentially private scree estimates using these control options. plot.dp_scree() for plotting scree estimates.

Examples

huber_control(k_min_m2 = -10, k_max_m2 = 10, m2_frac = 1 / 4)
#> $mu0
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $eta0
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $T
#> NULL
#> 
#> $M
#> NULL
#> 
#> $k_min_m2
#> [1] -10
#> 
#> $k_max_m2
#> [1] 10
#> 
#> $m2_frac
#> [1] 0.25
#>
